manifest.name: dsh-playwright-cli
manifest.description: Drive a real browser from DeepSeek Harness: microsoft/playwright-cli as one token-efficient tool plus a bundled skill.
manifest.author: chenxuuu

bundle.text:
# Bundle patch layer: one Host row that registers the `playwright_cli` tool and
# the bundled `playwright-cli` skill. Every field below is optional; the defaults
# are shown so they are discoverable in this file.
- insert:
    - id: playwright-cli
      name: dsh-playwright-cli
      config:
        # Absolute path to `playwright-cli.js` (run with `nodePath`) or to a real
        # executable. Omit it to auto-discover a local/global installation.
        # executable: C:\Users\you\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\@playwright\cli\playwright-cli.js
        # Node.js executable used to run the CLI entry (default: the Harness Node).
        # nodePath: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe
        # Default named browser session; the `playwright_cli` tool can override it.
        session: ''
        # Per-command wall clock limit in milliseconds.
        timeoutMs: 120000
        # Keep the CLI's update banner off: it writes to stderr and, on Node 24,
        # the notifier crashes the process after the command already succeeded.
        disableUpdateNotifier: true
        # Extra environment for every CLI invocation.
        # env:
        #   PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BROWSER: chrome

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-playwright-cli)
[](LICENSE)

Drive a real browser from **DeepSeek Harness**: one tool, `playwright_cli`, wraps
[`microsoft/playwright-cli`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli), plus a bundled
`playwright-cli` skill that teaches the model the command vocabulary.

playwright-cli itself recommends *CLI + skills* over MCP for coding agents: commands are short, and
the page snapshot goes to a file instead of a giant tool schema or accessibility tree. This plugin
keeps that design and only adds the two missing pieces — a tool the model can call, and a skill that
is discovered and loaded on demand.

中文说明见 [README.zh.md](README.zh.md)。

**In the app:** **Plugins → Plugin Manager → install bundle → `dsh-playwright-cli`**.

**From a shell**, when the Harness CLI is on your PATH:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add dsh-playwright-cli
```

**From an agent:** `plugin_manager` with `action: install_bundle`, `target: dsh-playwright-cli`.

> PATH collisions are common on Windows (`dsh` may belong to another product). If `dsh plugin` is not
> the Harness CLI, use the in-app Plugin Manager.

`playwright-cli` must be available on the machine:

```bash
npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest
```

And a browser has to exist — playwright-cli ships none. Either download its Chromium once:

```bash
playwright-cli install-browser chrome-for-testing
```

or reuse a browser that is already installed, which needs no download at all:

```text
playwright_cli  open https://example.com --browser=msedge
```

```text
playwright_cli  open https://playwright.dev --browser=msedge
playwright_cli  snapshot --depth=4
   → [artifacts] C:\...\.playwright-cli\page-....yml   (read this file to get refs)
playwright_cli  click e15

Every result carries the page status, the artifacts it produced (absolute paths), and the CLI's exit
code. `--raw` returns just the value, e.g. `--raw eval "document.title"`.

| Parameter | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | yes | One playwright-cli command without the `playwright-cli` prefix. Quote arguments containing spaces. |
| `session` | no | Named browser session (`-s=<name>`), for isolating parallel tasks. |
| `workdir` | no | Working directory; artifacts land in `<workdir>/.playwright-cli/`. Defaults to the session directory. |
| `timeoutMs` | no | Per-call wall clock limit (default from config, capped at 900000). |
Every field is optional and lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` under the `playwright-cli` row:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executable` | auto-discovered | Absolute path to `playwright-cli.js` (run with `nodePath`) or to a real executable |
| `nodePath` | `node` from PATH | Node used for the CLI *and* the browser daemon it spawns |
| `session` | none | Default session name |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-command limit |
| `disableUpdateNotifier` | `true` | Sets `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` (see the Node 24 note below) |
| `env` | `{}` | Extra environment, e.g. `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BROWSER: chrome` |

- **No shell.** The command line is tokenized and passed as an argv vector to
  `node playwright-cli.js …`, so `&` in URLs, spaces in paths, `--data="k=v"` and Windows quoting
  cannot corrupt a command.
- **Discovery.** It walks up from the session directory looking for a local
  `node_modules/@playwright/cli` or `node_modules/playwright`, then checks the usual global npm,
  pnpm and Homebrew locations. `executable` overrides all of it.
- **Real Node, not the Host binary.** The desktop Host runs as Electron-as-node
  (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`), so `process.execPath` is the app binary. playwright-cli re-spawns its
  browser daemon with that path and dies with `too many arguments`; the plugin therefore resolves a
  real `node` from PATH first.
- **Exit codes are honest.** playwright-cli's update notifier crashes the process *after* a successful
  command on Node 24 (exit code becomes `0xC0000409`); the notifier is disabled by default.
- **Artifacts are files.** Snapshots, screenshots, PDFs, videos, traces and console logs are resolved
  to absolute paths and listed under `[artifacts]`, so the model reads them with `read` / `read_image`
  instead of paying for them in the result.
- *

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `playwright-cli is not installed or was not found` | no local/global install | `npm i -g @playwright/cli@latest`, or set `executable` |
| `Browser "chrome-for-testing" is not installed` | no bundled browser | `playwright_cli install-browser chrome-for-testing`, or `--browser=msedge` |
| `Chromium distribution 'chrome' is not found` | Chrome not in its default path | `--browser=msedge` or `--browser=chrome` |
| `too many arguments. Expected 1 argument but got 2` | CLI launched with the Electron binary | leave `nodePath` unset so the plugin resolves `node` |
| `The browser '<name>' is not open` | session idle-closed or never opened | `open` again (add `--persistent` to keep the profile) |
| `百度安全验证` page on Baidu | site-level anti-automation captcha | not a plugin bug: report the wall, try another engine |
| snapshot only has header/footer | results rendered after the command returned | re-run `snapshot`, or use `find "<text>"` |

| Path | Owns | Update it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Tool schema, spawn, discovery, artifacts, hints, presenters | CLI flags/output shape change, or DSH's `ToolDefinition` changes |
| `skill.js` | Model-facing skill text (command table, loop, triage) | the command surface changes |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Loader row + default config + field comments | you add a config key |
| `locale/*.json`, `icon.svg` | Plugin Manager title, description, icon | wording/branding |
| `README.md`, `README.zh.md` | user + maintainer docs | any behavior change |

readme.section: Adapting to a new playwright-cli release
readme.text:
1. `npm view @playwright/cli version`, then `npm i -g @playwright/cli@latest`.
2. `playwright-cli --help` — compare the command list with the table in `skill.js`. The skill *is* the
   model's contract, so keep it in sync before anything else.
3. Check `open` / `attach` flags (`--browser`, `--device`, `--persistent`, `--profile`, `--config`).
   New flags normally need docs only, no code.
4. Check the output markers: `### Page`, `### Snapshot`, `[Snapshot](.playwright-cli/…)`, `### Events`
   with `console-….log#L1-L6`. If a path shape changes, adjust `MARKDOWN_LINK`, `FILE_TOKEN` and the
   `#L…` stripping in `collectArtifacts()`.
5. Check session selection: the plugin passes `-s=<name>` **and** sets `PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION`. If a
   release starts rejecting one of them, drop the env assignment in `execute()`.
6. Check the error strings matched by `hintFor()`: `is not installed`,
   `Chromium distribution 'chrome' is not found`, `is not open, please run open first`.
7. Run the smoke test below, then bump the version and the changelog.

DSH validates the tool's returned value against `output.schema`; a mismatch fails the whole call with
`returned invalid output`. Declare every nullable field as
`oneOf: [{type:'string'}, {type:'null'}]` (this bit us once with `signal: null`), and build the
returned object and the schema together.

readme.section: Adapting to a new DSH release
readme.text:
1. `dsh --version`; only raise `engines.dsh` when you depend on something new.
2. Re-check the four services the plugin uses. In a live session: `cordis_inspect_query` with
   `platform: host`, `provider: Service`, `input: {"service":"tools"}` (also `subprocess`, `skills`,
   `workingDirectory`).
3. Confirm `ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable('node')` still resolves; if a Host stops running as
   Electron-as-node, the fallback to `process.execPath` keeps working either way.
4. This plugin intentionally ships **no `Config` schema** (it would add a schemastery dependency). If
   in-app config editing starts requiring one, add `export const Config`.
5. Reinstall and confirm both halves registered: the tool in the agent's tool list and
   `playwright-cli` in the skill catalog.

Semver: **patch** = docs/hints, **minor** = new commands or config keys (backward compatible),
**major** = renamed package/row, removed config, renamed tool.

```bash
npm pack --dry-run          # confirm index.js, skill.js, patch, locale, icon, docs, LICENSE
git add -A && git commit -m "release: vX.Y.Z"
git tag vX.Y.Z && git push --follow-tags
npm publish                 # add --provenance when publishing from CI

Then verify from a clean state:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-playwright-cli
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-playwright-cli
```

and run the smoke test. Keep `CHANGELOG.md` current.

The profile links this directory, but the Host caches the loaded module. After editing `index.js`,
`skill.js` or `cordis.patch.yml`, remove and re-install the bundle (Plugin Manager toggle, or
`remove_bundle` + `install_bundle` through `plugin_manager`); only a reload picks up new code.

| Command | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `--version` | version line, `exit=0` |
| `list` | `(no browsers)` or the open sessions |
| `open https://example.com --browser=msedge` | page title, `.playwright-cli/page-*.yml` artifact |
| `find "Example"` | matching nodes with context |
| `screenshot --filename=shot.png` | `shot.png` under absolute `[artifacts]` |
| `close` | `Browser '<name>' closed` |

Search-engine smoke tests are the honest end-to-end check: Bing/Google work headless; Baidu returns a
captcha page to automation and should be reported, not retried.

1. Replace the placeholders in `package.json`: `YOUR NAME`, `YOUR_GITHUB_USER` (three URLs).
2. `git init && git branch -M main`, create the GitHub repository, push.
3. `npm login` (2FA accounts need an OTP), then `npm publish`.
4. Publish must go to the public npm registry; mirrors such as `registry.npmmirror.com` are for
   *installing*, not for `npm publish`.
5. Optional: publish from GitHub Actions with `--provenance` (`id-token: write`), or configure npm
   trusted publishing for the repository.

readme.section: Getting listed in the in-app market
readme.text:
Direct install by package name works as soon as the package is on npm. The **Plugin Market**
(`dshmarket`) reads a curated catalog, `https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json`, fetched fresh on
every request; entries carry `name`, `description`, `category` (at least one), and a `source`
(`npm` package or URL/repo). Listing is curated — submit an entry to that catalog (its repository
accepts PRs/issues for new plugins) with:

readme.section: Getting listed in the in-app market
readme.text:
```json
{
  "name": "dsh-playwright-cli",
  "description": "microsoft/playwright-cli as a DSH tool plus a bundled skill.",
  "category": ["tool", "browser"],

Users can also add that catalog URL manually under **Plugins → Discover → Index sources**.

MIT for this plugin. The skill text in `skill.js` is adapted from
[`microsoft/playwright-cli`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli)'s `SKILL.md`
(Apache-2.0, Copyright Microsoft Corporation); see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
